subject.title: [Feature]: Add portable Agent Bundles for export/import across OpenClaw instances

question: Should OpenClaw core own a first-class portable agent bundle import/export contract, and what non-secret manifest, workspace, skill, binding, and environment-requirement fields should it allow?
rationale: The request crosses core config, gateway protocol, workspace writes, plugin/skill install, and security boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose core-versus-plugin ownership or the import trust model.

options.title: Core portable bundle contract
options.body: Add a preview or dry-run-first core CLI/RPC surface with manifest validation, explicit portable allowlists, and secret/runtime-artifact exclusions.

options.title: Plugin or ClawHub proof first
options.body: Keep core limited to missing APIs and let a bundle-style plugin prove agent packaging until core sponsorship is clearer.

options.title: Fold into broader migration design
options.body: Track this under cross-platform migration or per-agent backup/restore if maintainers want one archive model for portability, restore, and clone flows.

recommendation.title: Core portable bundle contract
recommendation.body: Add a preview or dry-run-first core CLI/RPC surface with manifest validation, explicit portable allowlists, and secret/runtime-artifact exclusions.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing agent create/update/delete RPC work is the most central current surface a bundle importer would need to extend.
